title: Operational deviation from an Instance Configuration Document invalidates that Instance's RRC and the Prime's Aggregate RRC
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.5 opens with a consequence that is easy to underrate: "Operational deviation from Artifact specifications can render an Instance's RRC, and thus the Prime's Aggregate RRC, invalid."

RRC is computed from declared parameters — target chains, protocols, maximum deposit sizes and the rest of the Operational Parameters listed in A.2.2.10.1.1.2.1.3.3. If an Instance operates outside those parameters, the calculation's inputs no longer describe reality, so the output stops being a capital requirement and becomes an arbitrary number.

The propagation is what makes this severe. Aggregate RRC is the sum of Instance Total RRCs and is "the figure against which a Prime Agent's Total Risk Capital (TRC) adequacy is assessed" (A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.1.1). One non-conforming Instance therefore invalidates the denominator of the Prime's entire solvency test — and every downstream artifact built on it, including the OVRC comparison and the TRC Report's ratio computations.

This is why conformance monitoring is mandated regardless of who operates the Instance: "Whether a Prime self-operationalizes its Allocation System or contracts with an Operational Executor Agent, its Agent Artifact must define processes for monitoring for, and addressing deviations of, Instance operational conformance." A self-operationalizing Prime keeps its strategy private but cannot opt out of proving it stayed inside the declared envelope.
description: The consequence is measurement failure, not just added risk: once actual operation departs from the specified parameters, the capital requirement computed from them no longer describes the position.
